d.d: simple past and past participle of up
At a higher physical position, level, rank or order.
Situated on higher ground, further inland, more upstream, or more northerly.
A stimulant, such as amphetamine, that increases energy and decreases appetite.
A swinging blow aimed upwards at the opponent's chin.
A cut shot that sends the ball over the wicket-keeper's head.

d.x: The bowler was bowling a bouncer so he uppercut the ball for six.

d.d: At or nearest the top of something.
d.x: She couldn't reach the bowls on the uppermost shelf, so she made do with a mug.

d.d: The parts of a pair of shoes that do not normally contact the ground.
d.x: His shoes were so worn that he was walking on his uppers.

d.d: present participle and gerund of up
Presumptuous, above oneself, self-important; arrogant, snobbish, haughty.
Exceeding one's station or position, assuming prerogatives to which one is not entitled.
